Yes, MathOp's operator supports 'sqrt'. No, it does not support 'atan' (it supports 'tan' but there is no 'atan').

Per the AccessorOp source/description: d (current data row), i (row index), data (all rows), op() (function to access operators), sequenceTime (timeline position), frame (current frame), totalFrames (total frames), sequence (timeline metadata), plus utility globals like d3 and turf.

MapStyleOp was removed (schema migration 014-remove-map-style-op). It was a pass-through node exposing a preset map style URL; the migration deletes MapStyleOp nodes and inlines their mapStyle URL value onto the connected MaplibreBasemapOp's mapStyle input (falling back to CARTO_DARK if no value), removing the node and its edges.
Migration 006 renamed the Theatre timeline sheet ID in timeline.sheetsById from 'Nodes' to 'Noodles' (preserving all other timeline state); it did not rename any operator nodes.
Migration 013 added time-markers support to the timeline: it initializes an empty markers array (sequence.markers = []) on the timeline's Noodles sheet sequence for projects that lack one.
NOODLES_VERSION is computed as the max migration number, which is currently 14 (highest migration file is 014). Note: AGENTS.md text says version 6, but the code's actual current version is 14.
'@/' is the projectScheme prefix meaning the path is relative to the project's data directory (project assets); FileOp reads such URLs from the current project's assets.
Unix-style fully qualified paths, e.g. '/my-node' at root or '/container/child' for nested nodes.
The sibling operator in the same container as the current operator.
By an absolute path that includes the container, e.g. '/analysis/filter' (or '/container/child').
